notes:
FICTIONAL PATIENT FOR SOFTWARE TESTING ONLY

Patient: Synthetic Tessa Calder
Clinic record number: SYN-TC-1017
Age and sex: 43-year-old woman
Date of service: 17 October 2026
Treating clinician: Dr. Samira Voss
Encounter: New-patient, in-person visit in a U.S. gastrointestinal office.
New-patient history: During the preceding three years, she has received no professional services from Dr. Voss or from any physician or qualified health professional of the same specialty and subspecialty in this same group practice. The earlier family-medicine visit described below was at an unrelated practice.

S - Subjective
Synthetic Tessa Calder reports esophageal dysphagia for six weeks and heartburn for four months. Two or three times a week, bread or meat feels stuck behind her lower sternum after she swallows. The sensation settles within several minutes after sips of water. Her heartburn occurs about three evenings per week, usually after the evening meal.
She denies difficulty initiating a swallow, difficulty swallowing liquids, painful swallowing, vomiting, vomiting blood, black stools and unintentional weight loss. She has not had a food impaction requiring an emergency intervention.
On 20 August 2026 she saw Dr. Nora Hale, a family-medicine clinician at an unrelated primary-care practice, for heartburn. Dr. Hale recommended a 14-day trial of omeprazole 20 mg by mouth once daily. She took it from 21 August through 3 September 2026. It partially reduced her heartburn, but she developed headaches. She stopped omeprazole on 3 September because of the headaches; the headaches resolved after stopping. She is no longer taking omeprazole. This was an outside primary-care visit, not a previous visit with Dr. Voss or this GI group.
Her current medication is famotidine 20 mg by mouth each evening for heartburn, started on 18 September 2026. Her relevant medical history is seasonal allergic rhinitis. She has no known previous esophageal disease, no history of upper gastrointestinal surgery and no prior upper endoscopy. Her documented medication allergy is trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, which caused an itchy rash.

O - Objective
Blood pressure is 116/72 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius and weight 64.2 kg. She appears comfortable and clinically stable. The oropharynx is moist without a visible lesion. The abdomen is soft and nontender, with normal bowel sounds and no guarding or rebound. The abdominal examination is stable and unchanged on repeat examination at the end of this same visit, compared with the initial examination today.

A - Assessment
Esophageal dysphagia and heartburn were both evaluated today. The underlying etiology remains uncertain. Reflux-associated mucosal irritation and a structural esophageal cause are considerations, not established diagnoses. No definitive underlying disease is diagnosed at this visit.

P - Plan
Upper endoscopy is ordered today for a later outpatient appointment to investigate the esophageal dysphagia and heartburn. It was not performed today, and no upper-endoscopy results are available. No procedure was performed during this encounter.
No medication change is made today. The plan is to arrange the ordered investigation and record symptom frequency while awaiting it. Follow-up is planned after the endoscopy to discuss its findings, with earlier contact if symptoms worsen.

Office E/M selection is based on total physician time on the date of service. Dr. Voss personally spent 47 minutes on 17 October 2026: seven minutes reviewing the available outside records, 31 minutes obtaining the history, performing the examination and counseling the patient, and nine minutes entering the investigation order and documenting the encounter. These are all physician activities on the encounter date. The 47 minutes exclude eight minutes of staff intake work and six minutes of physician record review performed on the preceding day. The total also excludes any time for separately reported services.
